title: OpenAI-compat: tool schema inference + streaming coalescer for robust tool_choice semantics
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: customers using the OpenAI compatibility layer can send mixed tool definitions (partial schemas, polymorphic args, and aliasing). The old mapper required explicit, fully-specified signatures and emitted multiple ambiguous tool_choice messages during streaming, which caused downstream tool runners to drop or duplicate invocations under backpressure. This PR implements two coordinated improvements: (1) a Conservative Schema Inference pass that synthesizes a normalized ToolDescriptor from partial OpenAI tool specs while preserving semantic hints (aliases, required/optional, value-allowlists). Inference rules prefer strictness for safety but attach a provenance tag so the runtime can choose relaxed matching at call time; (2) a Stream Coalescer in the OpenAI-compat bridge that groups fragmentary function/tool frames across streaming boundaries, repairs broken JSON fragments, and emits canonical tool_choice events only once the inferred signature confidence crosses a threshold. Changes: new inference heuristics, confidence scoring, provenance metadata, streaming buffer/coalescing logic, metrics and congestion metrics for tool_choice events, and an upgraded test matrix (unit + integration + e2e) against a simulated tool-runner with backpressure. Migration/compatibility: old behavior preserved behind a feature flag (openai_compat.infer_schema=true). For customers who relied on the previous permissive mapping we provide a toggle and a short compatibility shim. Rationale: this reduces duplicate tool invocations, decreases false-positive tool matches when tools have overlapping arg shapes, and stabilizes streaming tool invocations in lossy networks. The description below summarizes the scope of changes, CI, and review notes.

review_conversation: Jonas Kim (reviewer): Nice direction — main question is around performance: can the inference pass scale to high QPS without adding tail latency? Please add microbenchmarks.

Maya Patel (author): Added microbenchmarks under runtime/bench/infer_bench_test.go and a config knob to cap inference CPU budget. Coalescer is asynchronous and will prioritize forwarding when confidence is low to avoid stalls.
Ava Rodriguez (reviewer): I requested a stronger audit trail for inferred fields. Please add provenance tags for each synthesized argument so we can exclude inferred params from privacy exports.
Maya Patel (author): Added provenance_tags.go and wired tags through dispatch. Also updated observability to mark inferred keys in traces and metrics.
Diego Martinez (reviewer): Found a race in coalescer buffer; suggested an RW mutex and a clearer shutdown path for streaming sessions.
Maya Patel (author): Fixed race by switching to a session-scoped channel and added a graceful drain in coalescer.Shutdown; added tests simulating abrupt disconnects.

Jonas Kim (reviewer): Approving after microbenchmark results look stable (p50 unaffected, p99 +3ms under pathological aggregation).
release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: added conservative schema inference for partial tool definitions and a streaming coalescer to reduce duplicate/ambiguous tool_choice emissions. Defaults preserved behind feature flag openai_compat.infer_schema. Improves streaming stability and reduces duplicate invocations under backpressure.
notes: This PR touches the compatibility bridge and runtime streaming path. Ops: enable feature flag globally after a canary in production for 48h. Rollback: flip openai_compat.infer_schema=false to revert to previous permissive mapping.
egress_examples: Before: client sent fragmented tool frames and runtime occasionally emitted duplicate tool_choice events leading to repeated tool runs.
After: coalescer reassembles fragments, inference provides a normalized signature with provenance, and a single tool_choice event is emitted once confidence threshold is met.
